workstreams.autoTitle: New sessions get their own workstream

workstreams.prefixFootnote: Only affects new workstreams. Existing branches keep their names — rename one from the bar under the composer.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.title: Send anonymous usage data
privacy.description: Counts and timings — app launches, finished turns, how many steps and tools a turn took, how many tokens it used and roughly what it cost — tied to a random id generated on this machine. Never your prompts, your code, file paths, repo names, or any error text.
privacy.labels: A few labels ride along, and each is matched against a fixed list built into the app: which provider served a turn (a custom endpoint is only ever recorded as “other”), which model family ran (“claude-sonnet”, never the exact model id), which built-in tools ran (an MCP server's own name is only ever recorded as “mcp”), and which kind of error ended a failed turn. It is the only way we can tell whether a release helped or broke things.

themes.title: Themes
themes.subtitle: A theme is a small JSON file that re-points the app’s design tokens — surfaces, text, accents, and the fonts for the UI and for code. Pick one below, or duplicate it to make your own. Themes are read from your themes folder, so they can be edited in any editor, checked into dotfiles, and shared as a file.
themes.emptyLead: No custom themes yet. Duplicate one above to get a file you can edit, or drop a
themes.reappliesHint: Saving re-applies the theme if it’s the active one.
themes.buildWithAiBody: Copies a full spec of this format — every token, what it paints, the rules and a worked example. Paste it into any model, describe the theme you want, and drop the JSON it returns into the editor.
themes.colorsBody: Any CSS color — hex, rgb(), oklch(), or a color-mix(). Anything you leave out is inherited from the theme you extends, so a theme can be three lines long.
themes.fontsBody: sans is the UI font and mono is the code font — tool calls, terminal output, diffs and code blocks. Give one family, an array to build your own stack, or "system" for the platform’s native font. Fallbacks are appended automatically, so naming a font you don’t have degrades gracefully.
